why: The statement names the Fujita conjecture, which has two parts (freeness at m >= n+1, very ampleness at m >= n+2), so a proof of freeness alone is a case (F3), not whole; the OpenAI manuscript explicitly disclaims very ampleness. openai-2026 and openai-math-038 are the same manuscript recorded twice and get identical answers. It is unreviewed and doubtful but not not_credible: there is no identified error, and three to eight days of silence is too short to count as missing uptake. Its AI role is generated: the repository says the manuscripts were produced by an internal model, and the author line is just 'OpenAI'. The basis is a collection-level 'vast majority' sentence, though. Han's ChatGPT acknowledgement covers sharpness examples for an appendix corollary that the main bound (Theorem 1.1) does not use, so the bound event is none. Chan is knocked_down by withdrawal. Siu 2026 is treated as a very-ampleness bound and counted digested because a journal of record published it. Conditional results (BBMT, Benammar) are none. Different-setting results (char p, 2K+mL, convex Fujita numbers, the K+aK+bL variant, singular T-varieties, the m=1 volume-hypothesis result) are variant. Dimension-specific proofs are case and sharp-threshold-in-n bounds are bound.
doubts: AI attribution for the OpenAI manuscript rests on a repository-wide 'vast majority' sentence, not a per-manuscript statement. Han's ai_role is a close call: ChatGPT suggested constructions that appear in the paper (assisted on a strict reading), but they support only a sharpness corollary, not the freeness bound that bears on this problem. Siu 2026's content is unread, so its scope as a bound is inferred from a talk abstract. The reduction from compact complex manifolds with positive L to projective varieties via Kodaira is the researcher's, though it is standard.
